title: Reading how many times from range
idea: MEET. For count-controlled problems, read the repeat count straight from range(n) / range(start,stop) / range(start,stop,step). Thinking, no writing.

exercises.explanation: range(4) starts at 0 and stops BEFORE 4: 0,1,2,3 — four values, so the loop runs 4 times.

exercises.prompt: How many times does a for loop over range(4) run its body?
exercises.explanation: Four values (0,1,2,3) means four repeats. range(n) always runs n times.
range(start, stop) begins at 2 and stops before 6: 2,3,4,5 — four values.
From 2 up to but not including 6 is 2,3,4,5 — four values, so four repeats. (stop minus start.)
Start at 1, step by 2, stop before 10: 1,3,5,7,9 — five values.

exercises.prompt: range(0) runs its loop body zero times.
exercises.explanation: True. range(0) is empty — no values — so the body never runs. A good edge case to remember.

exercises.prompt: You need a loop that runs exactly 7 times. Which range?
exercises.explanation: range(7) gives 0..6, seven values — exactly 7 repeats. range(1,7) is only 6.

exercises.prompt: Match each range to how many times it repeats.
exercises.explanation: range(3): 0,1,2. range(5,8): 5,6,7. range(0,10,2): 0,2,4,6,8. Count the values to get the repeats.
range(10) is 0..9, ten values. range(1,10) is only 9; range(10,20,2) is 5; range(0,5) is 5.

exercises.prompt: Why read the range carefully before trusting a count?
options: range stops BEFORE the stop value, so it is easy to be off by one
exercises.explanation: range never includes the stop value, so 'off by one' mistakes are common. Count the values to be sure.
